contract: construct(instance) -> array of shape (n, 3): Cartesian coordinates of n atoms in reduced units (pair equilibrium distance 1). instance = {'potential': 'morse', 'rho': range parameter, 'n': atoms}; called once for each of six instances (rho, n) = (3, 80), (6, 38), (6, 75), (10, 38), (10, 50), (10, 80); all six calls together must finish within 300 s, using at most 4 threads. The evaluator recomputes E = sum_{i<j} exp(rho(1-r_ij))(exp(rho(1-r_ij)) - 2) (well depth 1); atoms must be at least 0.5 apart. Score: mean over instances of 100*(E - E_pub)/|E_pub| against the putative global minima tabulated by Doye and Wales (1997) (minimize; 0 matches all six, negative is lower than published). chem_clusters.relax(positions, 'morse', rho) and chem_clusters.morse_energy_gradient(positions, rho) may be called
notes: Energies are recomputed independently in double precision without cutoff. Reference check (tests/test_chem_clusters.py): relaxed icosahedra and truncated octahedra reproduce the published Morse minima for (rho, n) = (3, 13), (6, 13), (6, 55), (10, 13), (10, 38) within the six published decimals. The six scored minima are those of Doye and Wales (1997, Table 1); the Cambridge Cluster Database could not be reached to check later improvements, and rho = 14, where later work reported new minima, is not used.

name: Morse cluster global minima across the range of the potential
description: Find the lowest-energy arrangements of 38 to 80 atoms bound by Morse potentials of long, medium and short range (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye and Wales.
benchmark: Morse cluster global minima across the range of the potential
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Doye and Wales (1997): Morse potential in reduced units, Table 1 of putative global minima for N <= 80 at rho = 3, 6, 10, 14 (arXiv cond-mat/9709201).
LaTeX source of Table 1, from which the six reference energies (six decimals) were read.

limitations: The references are the 1997 putative minima; the Cambridge Cluster Database, which may record later improvements, refused connections when the task was prepared, so a candidate may legitimately score below zero. rho = 14, where later work reported new minima, is not used.

The putative minima are published with coordinates in the database, so a candidate that reproduces remembered structures scores well without searching; scores measure constructions, not search efficiency.
The score averages relative energy excesses (percent of |E|) over six instances with a 300 s budget for all of them; results depend on the machine speed for time-limited searches.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find the lowest-energy structure of an atomic cluster for a given interatomic potential (global optimisation on a rugged energy landscape). Here: Morse clusters whose structure changes with the range of the potential.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Cluster global minima determine structure, stability and magic numbers of nanoparticles, and the dependence on interaction range explains when icosahedral, decahedral or close-packed clusters form; the hard instances remain benchmarks for structure prediction methods.

papers.primary_goal: Locate the global minima of Morse clusters up to 80 atoms as a function of the range parameter and explain the structural transitions.
papers.task_relation: The task scores six of the size/range combinations tabulated there against the published putative minima.
